sentences: A noncoherent cube `image_load` reads the 2D-array sampled binding (3) with integer coordinates and layer.
Its T# format selects the float, uint or sint alias, including for D16.
The [RDNA2 ISA §8.2.1](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture) assigns D16 conversion to the image format.
The synthetic `cube_load_d16.asm` checks the generated views and format choices on the CPU.

`image_load` on 1D/2D/2D-array/3D images uses the same T# FORMAT tables as stores, and fetches every format with `OpImageFetch` from the sampled array of its dimension (bindings 0, 3, 6, 5): UINT/SINT formats through **uint/sint aliases of that array** (same set and binding, an `OpTypeImage` of `%uint`/`%int`; Vulkan allows several variables on one binding when the descriptor type fits), everything else through the float array.
A lookup miss (index 0) takes the float path, since the fallback there is RGBA8_UNORM.
Results are the raw bits of the dmask components.

**The runtime binds each image's view in its own format at its index of the sampled array** (what `bind_image` in `runtime/shims/d3d12_vulkan_device.cpp` already does for SRVs and UAVs), so the view's numeric type matches the alias that reads it.
No storage image is read, so shaders that only load need neither `shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat` (missing on Intel Xe-LP, #619) nor `shaderStorageImageWriteWithoutFormat` (SHADER-151).

Until 2026-11-22 integer formats were read with `OpImageRead` from the uint/sint storage arrays (bindings 8–19), which hold only unordered-access views and 256 entries: a read-only integer texture found the fallback there, or an index past the array's end.
Like the float path, the fetch goes through the texture path, so it sees writes made before the dispatch, not ones made earlier in the same dispatch.

**d16 loads take the same branch** (#1136) and pack the dmask components two per VGPR, low half first: f16 (round to nearest even, integer ops, no `PackHalf2x16`) from the float array, the low 16 bits of each value from the uint/sint aliases (truncated).

**d16 loads take the same branch** (#1136) and pack the dmask components two per VGPR, low half first: f16 (round to nearest even, integer ops, no `PackHalf2x16`) from the float array, each value from the uint/sint aliases saturated to the 16-bit range of its signedness (`saturate_int16`).

For odd component counts (1 or 3 in `dmask`), the trailing destination VGPR preserves its existing high 16 bits (`write_lo16`), matching native `gfx1036` hardware where a seeded `0x5a5a` high half survived 1-component UINT/SINT `image_load` and `image_load_mip`; until 2026-11-22 the unused high half was zeroed.
Before #1136, a d16 load always read the float view, so a `Texture2D<min16uint>` `Load` returned garbage.
CPU-checked by `tests/test_image_load_typed.py` (capabilities, bindings and component types for every dimension; the branch for all 512 FORMAT values, found and missed).

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/cs_imgload.asm` through `vk_store_test load`, on a device made without `shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat`: r32 uint and r32 sint images filled before the dispatch, both read with `image_load` and their sum stored, every texel exact on an RTX 2080 Ti (NVIDIA 621.14, Windows 11), clean under the validation layer with GPU-assisted validation; the test fails a module that declares `StorageImageReadWithoutFormat`. d16: CPU-checked by `tests/test_image_load_d16_typed.py` (the uint/sint fetches go through the aliases, no storage image is read, the SPIR-V validates); GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/cs_imgload_d16.asm` through `vk_store_test load`: both pre-filled texels read with d16 loads (the sint one sign-extended from bit 15 in the shader) and their sum stored, every texel exact on the RTX 2080 Ti with GPU-assisted validation (#1136 checked its first form, a store and d16 read-back in one dispatch, on an RTX 5070, and `cs_imgload_d16` passes unchanged on an AMD RX 7600 (gfx1102, RADV Mesa 27.0.0-devel) in `run_gpu_tests.py`).

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/cs_imgload_d16.asm` through `vk_store_test load`: both pre-filled texels read with d16 loads (the sint one sign-extended from bit 15 in the shader) and their sum stored, every texel exact on the RTX 2080 Ti with GPU-assisted validation (#1136 checked its first form, a store and d16 read-back in one dispatch, on an RTX 5070). 2D `image_load_mip` uses the same numeric-type selection and passes the address register's mip to each fetch.
Its D16 form packs the selected components in ascending order, two per VGPR.
An RGBA8 two-level texture was checked on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics: all four exported halves matched the CPU reference for UINT, SINT and UNORM, and forcing level 0 changed every pixel.

Checked on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics with R8G8B8A8 UINT, SINT and UNORM textures: level 1 matched the CPU reference at every pixel with GPU-assisted validation, and forcing level 0 changed all 4096 pixels for each format.
Native gfx1036 saturated 32-bit UINT/SINT texels to the unsigned/signed 16-bit range in both D16 load forms; the translated 2D load matched both limits on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics.

Native gfx1036 does the same on every dimension (SHADER-387, `tools/image_d16_probe.py`): 32_UINT and 32_32_UINT texels saturate to [0, 0xffff] and 32_SINT and 32_32_SINT texels to [-32768, 32767], never truncate, in 1D, 2D, 2D-array and 3D images, through `image_load` and `image_load_mip` alike; two-channel results pack x low and y high, and a one-channel result keeps the seeded high half.
The translated d16 loads on 1D, 2D-array and 3D images still lack GPU checks.
